CO1: Sign and verify a message with the ECDSA equations on the chapter's curve, say which three inputs verification needs, and explain why exponents are reduced modulo n while coordinates are reduced modulo p
CO2: Decide, for each signature hash flag with and without ANYONECANPAY, which parts of a transaction a signature commits to, and explain the SIGHASH_SINGLE bug and how Bitcoin Core refuses it
CO3: Follow the step from an identity proof to a Fiat-Shamir signature and check a BIP340 signature: 64 bytes, an x-only key, a tagged hash and a default nonce
CO4: Explain why naive key aggregation fails (the key cancellation attack), what MuSig2 changes, and how Shamir secret sharing gives any two of three shares the secret and one share nothing
CO5: Judge the safety of a signing nonce: reuse, deterministic nonces by RFC 6979, low-R grinding and the size of a DER signature, with the Android random-number failure as the case
CO6: Separate what consensus requires of a signature from what relay policy requires (strict DER, low S, taproot hash types), and name what has changed in the standards and in Bitcoin Core since the book went to print
_serves: These six outcomes are chapter 8's: what a signature is and what it commits to (CO1, CO2), schnorr signatures and their aggregation (CO3, CO4), the safety of the nonce and the size of a signature (CO5), and how a node judges a signature and what has moved since print (CO6). The chapter serves LO-6 of the course (reading and constructing transactions, scripts and signatures and explaining how a node decides whether one is valid); CO2 and CO6 also touch LO-5 and LO-8 through the policy and security questions they raise.
